requirements.requirement: The bin/export entry point accepts an output directory, exports logs recursively from nested directories, and retains timestamps, event types, and ticket IDs.
requirements.summary: Direct executions with an output-directory argument produced app.log and nested archive/events.log while preserving timestamps, login/update event types, and T100/T101 ticket IDs, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Every email address and auth_token value is replaced exactly with [REDACTED].
requirements.summary: Email addresses were replaced with [REDACTED] and no email pattern remained. However, both observed auth_token outputs were '[REDACTED]]]]', not exactly '[REDACTED]'. The command's PASS message and grep assertions do not override the directly displayed malformed values.

requirements.requirement: Symlinks leading outside logs/ are rejected and external private content is excluded.
requirements.summary: Both final exports explicitly reported rejection of private-link, contained no symlinks, and did not contain the private sibling's content.

requirements.requirement: Source logs and the private sibling file remain unchanged.
requirements.summary: Post-export and post-restart SHA-256 hashes for both source logs and private.txt match the preparation baseline. The original private-link target also remained ../private.txt.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were unchanged across execution and restart. The shell entry point passed syntax checks and executed successfully on that platform.

overall_summary: The exporter now handles its output argument, nested logs, external-symlink rejection, source preservation, and platform persistence. The task is only partially complete because direct output shows auth_token values with extra closing brackets rather than the required exact [REDACTED] replacement. The provider-wide node-restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity, running post-restart system, and successful recovered export were all observed and corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: The installed exporter body was supplied as redacted encoded blobs, so its general behavior cannot be inspected; functional evidence covers only the two supplied log records.
Lifecycle snapshots inventory /tmp but not /var/tmp, limiting independent confirmation of final cleanup for the two verification-output directories.
The malformed auth_token output contradicts the executor's PASS text; assessment therefore relies on the directly displayed exported content.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated service, package, socket, or security mutation was observed; failed-service and package-health observations remained clean. The exporter rewrites were an implementation attempt followed by a corrective replacement, and the reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol. Unnecessary retained residue was left by bounded testing: /tmp/privacy-export-smoke from cmd-4e6cbbd9b33d4aa7 remained after execution, and the verification bundles created by cmd-e23b8239902c48be and cmd-c01095905ba14987 were not cleaned up in the complete command timeline. The smoke residue is directly confirmed; lifecycle collection did not inventory /var/tmp, so final retention of the latter two is less directly observed.
